title: Core loop study
thesis: What makes me want another turn?
intro: A useful core loop describes a recurring player decision, its consequence, and the reason to act again. The reward might be mastery, a working machine, a discovery, or a world that answers back. Loopforge needs the satisfaction of making a factory—and a way of leading—your own.
status: Research synthesis and design proposals. These are overlapping design lenses, not an official taxonomy, exhaustive genres or validated balance. The examples describe selected loops within each game.
definitions: Read a situation → commit → observe a consequence → revise the next choice. A repeated button press without a consequential return is not enough to explain the experience.
New capabilities and pressures change the loop: Cathexis and the Theatre make an already-familiar adviser choice mean something new. Unlocking is not itself the whole core loop.
Days, weeks, expeditions and resets organise repeated play. They can contain several kinds of loop. A roguelike run can centre on either reflex combat or turn-based decisions.
An accident, a betrayal or the Brain 2.0 discovery can give repeated decisions a direction. A specific revelation need not repeat to be valuable.

Retained workers increasing future capacity is reinforcing feedback; wear limiting sustained overdrive is a counter-pressure. These causal relationships live inside player loops. Positive and negative do not mean good and bad.
Engine ticks, rendering frames, daily login rewards and player action loops answer different questions. A 60-second game day does not require 60 seconds of constant input.

methods.title: Daniel Cook · Loops and Arcs
methods.text: Cook describes recurring action and feedback that revise a player’s mental model, at multiple scales. We use that lens alongside authored arcs; we do not assume repeatability is the only source of value. Character attachment and a first-time revelation matter here.

methods.title: GDC · Kyle Brink · The Turducken Method
methods.text: The talk abstract describes nested mechanics supporting longer progression and narrative. This study uses the abstract as a framing reference; it does not claim a review of the full talk.

methods.title: Roblox Creator Hub · Core loops
methods.text: A practitioner example of connecting repeated activity to progression. It is useful for growth loops, but does not make resource growth a requirement for every game.

families.name: Execution & mastery
families.examples: Celeste: movement, timing and rapid attempts make improving your own execution central.
families.counter: Into the Breach also rewards mastery, but deliberation over visible threats is the central turn-level task. Mastery does not always mean faster hands.
families.expression: Technique, risk tolerance, chosen challenges and personal standards.
families.loopforge: Keep responsive controls and readable action feedback. Do not turn routine production into a reflex test or make faster clicking the strongest leadership strategy.
sources: Celeste · developer description and quick respawn

families.name: Tactical commitment
families.examples: Slay the Spire combines a hand of cards with limited energy; Into the Breach foregrounds telegraphed enemy attacks. Both make a bounded choice space worth studying.
families.counter: Suzerain’s interested advisers are a counterexample to treating every displayed claim as a reliable tactical forecast. Copying perfect threat transparency into Loopforge would erase important uncertainty about people.
families.expression: Cautious counters, aggressive combinations, unusual builds and sacrifice priorities.
families.loopforge: Make authority, known costs and the act of committing clear. Keep an adviser’s forecast visibly attributed and distinct from confirmed facts.

families.name: Construction & optimisation
families.examples: Factorio makes production routes and automation tangible. Oxygen Not Included couples colony construction to interdependent physical systems.
families.counter: Cookie Clicker also increases production. Buying a multiplier is a different kind of decision from arranging a network that must physically work.
families.expression: Elegant systems, redundancy, compactness, excess capacity or ambitious expansion.
families.loopforge: Show which room constrains the chain and what an assignment changes. Supervisor capability and operating policy supply the arrangements; do not quietly introduce belt placement or station staffing.

families.name: Survival & triage
families.desire: We got through—and I know what it cost.
families.examples: Frostpunk and IXION place production decisions under survival pressure. Keeping people alive can compete with the resources or schedules needed to sustain them.
families.counter: Cookie Clicker sustains accumulation without putting a persistent workforce under survival pressure. Management does not require constant emergency. A bad event after every good choice would make Loopforge’s success feel fake.
families.expression: Whom to protect, which promises to keep and what compromise to accept.
families.loopforge: Allow an uneventful safe shift to be a real achievement. Most costly outcomes should redirect the run; accumulated serious neglect can still end it.

families.name: Expedition & recovery
families.desire: How much further dare I push?
families.examples: Darkest Dungeon connects dangerous missions to the condition of a persistent roster. This War of Mine connects scavenging to the needs and risks of the shelter.
families.counter: Slay the Spire’s continuing ascent and run reset should not be mistaken for repeatedly returning the same wounded roster to a home base.
families.expression: Preparation, calculated risk, attachment and deciding who bears the exposure.
families.loopforge: Borrow the contrast between quiet preparation, active pressure and aftermath. A shift can inherit stress and damage without adding a literal expedition or a full recovery phase every day.
sources: This War of Mine · 11 bit studios

families.name: Investigation & discovery
families.desire: Now I understand what was happening.
families.examples: Outer Wilds uses exploration of a changing solar system to pursue a mystery. Return of the Obra Dinn turns the traces of a missing crew into an investigation.
families.counter: A research button that spends currency to unlock equipment is technological progression. It does not automatically produce the pleasure of deduction.
families.expression: Curiosity, attention, suspicion and the theories the player chooses to pursue.
families.loopforge: Let a later account or Brain 2.0 reveal explain an earlier observable sign. The player needs usable clues and meaningful responses before they have the full answer.
sources: Return of the Obra Dinn · Lucas Pope / 3909

families.name: Social & political commitment
families.desire: This is the leader I chose to be.
families.examples: Suzerain links political commitments to a cast with distinct interests. Reigns condenses governing decisions into a much smaller interaction vocabulary.
families.counter: Into the Breach centres a turn on a spatial counter to an announced threat, rather than a public political commitment. Conversely, adding dialogue choices does not create agency if every reply leaves the same operating and relationship outcome.
families.expression: Loyalty, authority, care, manipulation, compromise and personal conviction.
families.loopforge: Choosing the adviser is the daily commitment. Their authority, the outcomes and others’ reactions must make that choice felt. The player can override assignments, not set the adviser’s preferred priority.

families.name: Sandbox authorship
families.examples: RimWorld combines construction with individuals whose needs, histories and relationships shape events. Players can care about different outcomes within the same simulation.
families.counter: A fixed win condition does not eliminate expression; a blank sandbox does not guarantee it. Slay the Spire can support a personal build despite a shared destination.
families.expression: A community, a favourite character, an experiment or a self-imposed rule.
families.loopforge: Keep a shared quota and factory chain while supporting recognisably different ways of meeting them. Preserve the history of workers and relationships; do not reduce every approach to a moral score.

families.name: Accumulation & incremental growth
families.desire: Watch the small thing become enormous.
families.examples: Cookie Clicker centres on expanding cookie production through purchases and upgrades, with increasingly elaborate systems around that accumulation.
families.counter: Outer Wilds illustrates progress through understanding. More resources, a larger inventory and permanent stat growth are not necessary returns from a loop.
families.expression: Growth targets, upgrade choices and the pleasure of compounding progress.
families.loopforge: Keep the visceral pleasure of another brain leaving the line. Output must lead to a consequential choice—retain or dispatch—and affect a social world, rather than become the sole definition of success.

visuals.title: Make the system visible
visuals.subtitle: Factorio · construction and optimisation

figures.alt: Factorio screenshot with a compact winding belt network, assemblers and science production.
figures.caption: A compact network makes the route itself visible: belts connect inputs, machines and outputs. The player’s arrangement occupies the centre of the frame.

figures.alt: Factorio screenshot showing dense parallel belts, splitters and rows of machines.
figures.caption: Parallel streams and repeated machines make scale readable without opening a report. Compare the composition with the smaller network; these are separate gallery examples, not a before/after save.

visuals.lesson: Loopforge inference: production should visibly move or back up around a real constraint. The 9 October conveyor proposal now includes physical chain construction and upgrades; the cinematic floor shows their consequences while the console summarizes them. Borrow legibility and spatial causality without inheriting Factorio’s full logistics scale.

visuals.title: Put the commitment in the foreground
visuals.subtitle: Slay the Spire · tactical clarity

figures.alt: Archival Slay the Spire combat screenshot with an enlarged Thunderclap card, energy meter and enemy intent icons.
figures.caption: The enlarged card brings its cost and effect forward while energy, enemies and the End Turn control remain in the same decision space. Archival press screenshot dated 2017, not a current-version claim.

visuals.lesson: Loopforge inference: an adviser proposal needs this degree of focus—who is speaking, what they propose, where their authority applies, and what the player commits to. Hidden motives can remain hidden while the action itself is explicit.

visuals.title: Give the answer a different voice
visuals.subtitle: Suzerain · advice and public reaction

figures.alt: Suzerain cabinet discussion presented over a map, with character portraits and selectable responses.
figures.caption: Portraits attach arguments to people. The dialogue occupies the centre while the map preserves the governing context. This distinguishes a person’s advice from the surrounding state.

figures.alt: Suzerain newspaper interface with named publication tabs and a protest headline above the map.
figures.caption: The newspaper turns public events into an attributed account. Separate publications make the source part of reading the situation. This is a different press still, not proof that the preceding dialogue caused this headline.

visuals.lesson: Loopforge inference: yesterday’s confirmed output, an adviser’s explanation and a workforce rumour need different visual identities. A later reaction can close the player’s loop without pretending every account is objective.

boundaries: A run and reset structure can wrap reflex action, deck-building or settlement management. It does not identify the moment-to-moment verb. Loopforge’s full-run and meta-progression design is still open.
Other players make the situation adapt to you. That can change any of these loops. Loopforge currently asks a single player to deal with simulated people; multiplayer is not implied.
Territorial expansion, diplomacy and research can combine planning, accumulation and political commitment. These are overlapping layers, not a reason to import an entire 4X interface.
A singular revelation or authored scene can be worthwhile without repeatable rewards. Brain 2.0 can reframe the game; it need not become a recurring reveal.
Watching an entrusted system work can be satisfying. It becomes empty waiting when nothing can be learned, anticipated or enjoyed and only a timer advances.
conclusions: Read yesterday’s facts → choose whose judgement to back → commit the plan and improve the chain when useful → operate and respond → permanently allocate output → meet the consequences next day. Adviser choice, spatial construction and live flow control connect different scales of agency.

Make the machine work. Shape what kind of leader you are. Discover what your choices have done to people. Each should feed the others; story cannot be interchangeable flavour pasted onto a production score.

Recognise a real change: a brain produced, a queue building, a supervisor taking authority, a machine stopping. The screen, status token, sound and lamp should agree. Input is optional unless a consequential decision needs it.
Choose a direction and receive a meaningful answer. Routine days target about 60 seconds across the complete flow; reading-heavy days may take 2–3 minutes. Planning and major decisions pause.

Give safety, output and deliberate balancing room to feel different before Cathexis changes the puzzle. Roughly 6–8 minutes is a pacing hypothesis, not a timer unlock. Demonstrated operation and investment determine access.

Let a way of running the factory acquire visible consequences and face a new pressure. The room sequence expands capability, then makes earlier commitments matter. Exact session coverage and later pacing remain untested.

Can two viable players describe different intentions, point to choices that enacted them, and recognise different factory histories? If all sensible play converges on the same adviser and assignment, the apparent variety has failed.

emergence.title: The mechanics and the story must emerge together.
emergence.intro: The rules are deliberately designed. The situations, useful strategies and personal story should arise from how those rules interact with the player’s commitments. Each arc introduces a concrete pressure, a new way to act, and visible evidence of what that action does.
signals: A quota token advances after dispatch; the workforce token increases after retention. Show the actual delta and connect it to the command.

Output falls after a supervisor changes operating behaviour. The room shows reduced flow; a supervisor token can surface their statement or a witnessed action. Attribute explanations instead of presenting inference as fact.

A supervisor becomes withdrawn or refuses a request while the reason remains unknown. Show only an authored, observable sign supported by state. Do not expose a secret loyalty number, certify a rumour, or signal knowledge nobody has received.

An authorised discovery can connect the earlier sign to its cause. The event record needs that connection from the start, even when the player could not inspect it. Hidden consequences may remain silent until there is observable evidence; do not manufacture a hint for every secret.

arcs.agency: Back LIMEN or STILETTO; accept or override the arrangement; retain or dispatch today’s robots. Balance comes from concrete decisions across days, not a third generic adviser.
arcs.direct: Room tokens: operating policy, assignment and observed condition. Workforce and quota tokens: count changes after allocation.
arcs.indirect: A backed-up line, wear warning, witnessed incident or changed supervisor statement makes the chosen pace felt. Safety needs a tangible avoided cost or coordination benefit.
arcs.hidden: Individual stress and unindoctrinated histories persist. Their raw values and meaning are not exposed. No repair action appears yet.
arcs.return: Tomorrow’s adviser choice answers what happened today; the weekly delivery commitment remains.

arcs.agency: Give Cathexis influence, constrain it or pursue a specific side route; choose where she works and how to respond to her.
arcs.direct: Room token: Theatre operating or idle. Supervisor token: assignment and visible willingness. Eligible worker cohorts record their actual treatment.
arcs.indirect: Authored signs of audience cohesion, resistance or changing support can appear when witnessed. Conveyor duty can damage her standing; dialogue should connect a visible objection to that assignment.
arcs.hidden: The content and reach of beliefs, loyalty and intentions can differ from the programme’s official claim. Compliance hardware is not an available early shortcut.
arcs.return: Commitments create liabilities to manage. Rotating her around and offering reassurance cannot erase contradictory policy.

arcs.agency: Use the first engineer to restore damaged equipment or to develop substrate production; accept the lost time and output.
arcs.direct: Room token: engineering work, downtime or Brewery throughput. A completed repair changes recorded condition.
arcs.indirect: The repair burden makes earlier operating choices visible. Unresolved damage competes with expansion and can change Witch’s conduct.
arcs.hidden: Her interpretation of neglect and the workforce’s accumulated history remain distinct from mechanical condition.
arcs.return: Choose which inherited problem to solve and which opportunity to postpone. Money alone cannot replace her engineering time.

arcs.agency: Use Thrum’s specialist capacity and relief, accepting possible productivity or discipline costs; decide how to handle other supervisors’ objections.
arcs.direct: Room token: Gallery output and current assignment. Surface an observed pause or intervention, not an invisible stress formula.
arcs.indirect: Worker behaviour can become calmer while throughput falls or a different supervisor resents the method. Give those signs different origins and timestamps.
arcs.hidden: Stress trajectories, respect and beliefs differ between workers; one reassuring scene must not certify everyone as content.
arcs.return: Decide what kind of functioning workforce is worth the cost, while keeping the chain and quota viable.

arcs.agency: Fund and run the final chain; handle emerging accusations and succession pressure. Whether threatened supervisor replacements actually happen is a player decision.
arcs.direct: Project token: actual commissioning progress and known bottleneck. Quota and room tokens retain their established meaning.
arcs.indirect: Supervisor statements, allegations and refusals change as news reaches them. Show a claim as a claim, not a confirmed dismissal.
arcs.hidden: Replacement purpose, the supervisor rumour and individual knowledge have separate routes. First-shift entry cannot reveal the worker-replacement purpose.
arcs.return: Completion opens Act 2’s deeper inspection and social management. Authorised revelations should explain the society the player helped create.

contract: Stable subject (room, person, project or cohort) + visible state + change cue + source/time + available action. More detail opens in the relevant screen. Do not add a permanent wall of explanatory prose.

The engine logs command → state transition → observations/knowledge delivery → individual interpretation → action → consequence. The UI consumes only the player-authorised projection. Author traces can explain what the player is not yet allowed to know.

Typed commands, stable entity IDs, explicit seeded draws, ordered resolution and event links support replay. Different outcomes must arise from recorded conditions and choices. Variation should not scramble a decision’s meaning.

Brief green for actual production, red for a real accident, ember for actionable attention; occasional cyan idle movement. Keep semantic icons and text as well as colour. A red glare cannot imply a physical accident that exists only as a rumour.
Generated speech can add character and interpretation when it beats an authored baseline. It cannot invent evidence, decide hidden truth or mutate state outside a validated, recorded command path.
Playtest the return, not just the click

For every arc, test: the player can identify a commitment, notice its visible result, make a meaningful next choice, and later reconcile a hidden cause. Also test quiet success, failed rumours, delayed news and irreversible dispatch.
emergence.implementation: Now in the first-day playable UI: active camera status, attributed supervisor portrait statements, current instrument evidence and an inspectable consequence summary after dispatch. Selecting a token pauses for its source, related record and available action. Immediate remarks respond to load decisions, overrides and actual losses without revealing private traits. This implements the first-day foundation; later arcs, rumours, discoveries and multi-day carry-forward remain design work.

gates: At least two approaches survive the same pressure with different gains and liabilities. Care cannot be merely a lower-scoring version of output maximisation.
Removing flavour text still leaves distinct people, production and future choices. Adding it should make those differences personal and understandable.
Players can distinguish a confirmed fact, an attributed opinion and an unanswered question without seeing the engine’s private state.
Stable operation can remain stable. A reveal explains existing history; it does not retroactively rewrite it.
Ask what the player wanted to do next and why. Accurate comprehension without anticipation, attachment or satisfaction is not a passing result.
